findings.description: The engine's only hook for goals, conversion definitions, targets and naming is a Markdown folder written by a coding agent for one company. Nothing in Makefile, seed, or the cloud app creates or selects such a folder, and the single FilesystemBackend root / single compiled graph means any file placed there is visible to every tenant's conversation. Capability-map and engine README list 'Read business context' as a capability; in this product it has no content. If used as designed with a real tenant's margins it would be a cross-tenant disclosure (P0 risk).
findings.recommendation: Model company context as an org-scoped record in adport's Postgres and inject it per turn (C3-01). Never populate the shared skills folder with any real tenant's data.

findings.title: Demo engine replays a hard-coded budget cut for any message matching a keyword regex, including the UI's own analysis suggestion

findings.description: WRITE_INTENT matches 'increase|raise|change|budget|…'. Still gated by adport approvals, so not P0; a live org that mapped a real account to alias 'demo-google' would receive a real pending budget cut from an analysis question (inferred risk).
findings.recommendation: Route the demo on explicit change verbs with a named target, echo the requested target/amount, and show the engine-mode banner independently of MARKTING_DEMO_MODE.

findings.title: Engine-side outcome memory is systematically wrong: every bridged proposal is recorded as rejected
evidence: rg "'expired'" platform/apps/cloud/lib platform/apps/cloud/app => markPendingOutcome('expired') never called
findings.description: After a successful preview the bridge immediately rejects the proposal on the engine ('handled by adport pending operation ...'), so pma_proposals.state becomes rejected and the LangGraph thread records a reviewer rejection even when adport later applies the change. findings.recommendation: Use a neutral hand-off decision (or a reject message the system prompt defines as 'pending human review in adport'); write the adport outcome back into the thread as a system message or injected context; set 'expired' from the retention sweep.

key_findings: Conversation memory exists only as LangGraph checkpoints (Postgres in compose, in-memory otherwise) and is write-only: no endpoint reads a thread back, listThreads is unused, and the UI loses the thread on reload.

Tenant isolation of conversations is enforced solely by a prefix check plus claimThread on the platform; the engine sees one caller 'adport-bridge' for all organizations, and the isolation DB test could not run here.

Two memory stores have no tenant boundary at all: the engine report index/files (GET /api/reports/engine* pass everything through) and the shared agent workspace/ArtifactStore readable and writable by every thread. Fixture-only data today; P0 the moment live reads are enabled.

Deleting an organization or applying data retention never touches engine-side checkpoints, pma_* rows or dedupe keys, which embed the deleted org's and user's UUIDs forever; no prune/delete code exists anywhere.

Engine outcome memory is systematically false: the bridge rejects every proposal on the engine after previewing it, so the engine and the conversation record 'rejected' even when adport applies the change; 'expired' is never written to provenance.

The only durable memory path (Postgres repositories and checkpointer) is unverified by tests in this checkout (skipped/ECONNREFUSED); two upstream contract tests fail because the markting host left engine/workspace/KILL_SWITCH in the shared workspace (confirmed by re-running with the path overridden).

No tenant, account, long-term or outcome memory exists; the upstream's MDA memory is off and documented as unsuitable where callers must not influence one another. Marketing Memory must be built on the adport side with per-org identity carried into the engine.

findings.title: Deep Agents summarization offloads evicted chat history into the shared filesystem root, readable by every other thread/organization
evidence: uv run --frozen python summ_probe.py => exit 0 (wrote conversation_history/sess-A.md under temp root; backend.ls and backend.read returned the verbatim human message)
findings.description: create_deep_agent unconditionally adds create_summarization_middleware(model, backend). For a plain FilesystemBackend its history prefix is /conversation_history and evicted messages are appended to /conversation_history/{session_id}.md via backend.write/edit, which bypasses tool-level filesystem permissions. In the markting host one process, one FilesystemBackend root and one graph serve every organization; the read-deny list does not cover /conversation_history, so any thread's model can `ls /conversation_history/` and `read_file` another organization's evicted chat. findings.title: Default demo engine leaks scripted-model state across threads; second thread gets 'exhausted' text or a malformed write turn
evidence: Runtime probe: threads A->ANALYSIS, B->EXHAUSTED, B(write)->'No receipt was returned: no tool result' (exit 0)
findings.description: LoopingScriptedChatModel is a single process-wide instance whose seen_human_messages counter is shared by all threads; it resets its script only when the human-message count differs from the last thread served. Any new thread whose first turn has the same count as the previous thread's last turn is served from an exhausted call_count and gets the 'offline demo engine' text; a write request in that state runs a trailing step without its predecessors. The Assistant creates a new thread per user/page load and the product defaults to MARKTING_ENGINE_MODE=demo. Host tests build a fresh app per test so never exercise two threads. findings.title: Default demo engine classifies analysis questions as change requests and stages a budget-cut proposal into adport's approval queue

findings.description: The shipped default model is a keyword regex (budget|reduce|lower|increase|raise|pause|change plus Arabic tokens). It matches 'changed', 'lower CPA', 'budget pacing', 'raised', the platform's own English suggestion chip ('increase'), and in Arabic the negation particle غير ('غير مستقر', 'ما الذي تغير') and زد inside 'يزداد'. Any match replays a fixed propose+execute script that stages a daily_budget 240 cut on g-103 regardless of the question; assistant.ts bridges it into PolicyEngine preview, a pending operation, an audit note and the Approvals page. Not unsafe execution (sandbox provider in demo mode, human approval required) but demo code reaching the production approval path; with MARKTING_DEMO_MODE=false and an org alias named demo-google the fixed proposal would map onto a real provider preview. The 7 host tests do not cover a mis-classified analysis question.
findings.recommendation: Do not infer intent from a substring regex: restrict the write script to explicit documented demo phrases (the chip text) or use anchored imperative-verb + object patterns with negation exclusion; use whole-word Arabic tokens with shadda (غيّر) and never bare غير/زد; add a regression test that every en/ar suggestion chip that is not a change request yields proposal=None.

findings.title: Model-call failures returned to the user as HTTP 200 answers (English error sentinel), not errors
evidence: runtime repro => assistant message 'Model call failed after 3 attempts with ValueError: ...'
findings.description: on_failure='continue' turns an exhausted model call into an AIMessage 'Model call failed after N attempts with <Type>: <msg>'. runner/outcome_view put it in outcome.text; app.py post_message returns 200; engine-client only treats non-2xx as errors; assistant.ts returns outcome.text verbatim; the chat UI renders it in a <pre>. Only admin/actions.py:1045 detects the sentinel and marks it a failure.
findings.recommendation: Propagate a typed failure (or detect the sentinel in runner/outcome_view as admin does) and map to 5xx with a localized message; have the engine-client/assistant surface an error state, not chat text.

findings.title: Deterministic/internal errors are retried as if transient, then swallowed
evidence: runtime repro: plain ValueError retried to exhaustion -> 'Model call failed after 3 attempts with ValueError'
findings.description: default_retry_on returns True for every non-ModelError exception, so config/programming errors (ValueError, KeyError, serialization, unwrapped auth/400) are retried MODEL_RETRY_ATTEMPTS+1 times with backoff and then masked as a model answer rather than failing fast.
findings.recommendation: Set an explicit retry_on limited to transient classes (timeouts/429/5xx); let deterministic errors propagate immediately, combined with C11-01 for surfacing.

findings.title: Nested retry layers and no per-request wall-clock cap
findings.description: SDK max_retries=2 nested inside ModelRetryMiddleware max_retries=2 (middleware timeout bounds each attempt at 120s); up to ~360s+backoff per inference, up to 40 model calls/run, with no overall engine request deadline.
findings.recommendation: Add a run-level wall-clock deadline and/or reduce stacked retries; align server worker timeouts to the realistic worst case.

findings.title: adport client timeout (240s) aborts while the engine keeps running (orphaned work, false 'unreachable')
findings.description: The client AbortController fires at MARKTING_ENGINE_TIMEOUT_MS (default 240s) and raises EngineError unreachable (503). A turn that exceeds that (C11-03) is not cancelled engine-side; it runs to completion (spending tokens) and advances the checkpoint while the user is told the engine is unreachable.
findings.recommendation: Honor client disconnect / enforce an engine deadline <= client timeout; return a resumable turn id for reconciliation.

findings.title: No per-thread concurrency control; duplicate/retried submissions race the checkpointer
findings.description: ThreadOwnershipStore.claim is ownership-only (returns True for the same caller every time), not a mutex; the message route carries no idempotency key. Two concurrent POSTs for the same thread (double-click, or a retry after the C11-04 abort) both call graph.ainvoke on the same thread_id, concurrently writing the LangGraph checkpoint. The reports endpoint uses an asyncio.Lock but message posting does not.
findings.recommendation: Serialize per thread_id (lock/DB advisory lock), reject a second in-flight turn with 409, and accept a client idempotency key.

findings.title: Catalog/provider outage at load is silently swallowed into a degraded surface, loaded once per process
findings.description: load_endpoint catches all exceptions and returns [], so a down/slow MCP endpoint (20s load timeout) drops its tools; the catalog is loaded once per process ('restart to pick up changes') and /health still reports status ok. The agent runs with a partial/empty read surface until manual restart.
findings.recommendation: Expose per-endpoint load status in health/metadata, fail boot or mark unhealthy when endpoints are missing, and add periodic catalog refresh with backoff. (Not reachable in the default fixture-catalog demo host.)

findings.title: Write-execution reliability is strong in code but not test-green here and unreachable in product
findings.description: One call_mutation attempt wrapped at 30s; ProviderTimeout/TimeoutError => outcome unknown with 'no retry was attempted'; idempotency key proposal:revision when configured; claim consumed (mark_used) with replay refusal before mutation; idempotent re-execute via cached receipt; bounded readback to an 'unknown' receipt. Correct anti-duplicate design, but the contract tests that assert it are red here (D1 kill switch) and the product swaps in ProposalOnlyWriteProvider so this path never runs a live write.
findings.recommendation: Make the kill-switch path hermetic in tests (resolve against workspace_root) so these contracts run green in CI.

findings.title: Streaming surfaces can duplicate partial text when a model call fails mid-stream and retries
findings.description: runner._run emits text events as the model streams; ModelRetryMiddleware re-invokes on failure; Slack delivery accumulates last_text += event.text, so an attempt-1 fragment then the attempt-2 full reply would both appear. The API/adport path is non-streaming and unaffected.
findings.recommendation: Reset per-attempt stream state on retry or buffer text until the attempt succeeds.

findings.title: Sync model-timeout path is a no-op (acceptable, documented)
findings.description: wrap_model_call (sync) returns handler(request) with no bound; the SDK timeout=120 is the only sync defense. All product surfaces use the async graph, so this is intentional; a future sync entrypoint would lose the hard cap against a post-headers gateway stall.
findings.recommendation: If a sync entrypoint is added, give it an equivalent hard bound.

key_findings: Model-provider outages surface to end users as HTTP 200 chat replies containing the English string 'Model call failed after N attempts with <Type>: <msg>' — no error status, no retry, no localization; only the admin console detects this sentinel, the API and Slack do not (C11-01).

The retry middleware treats ALL non-ModelError exceptions as retryable (default_retry_on), so deterministic/config errors are retried 3x with backoff and then masked as a model 'answer' — verified at runtime with a ValueError (C11-02).

Retries are stacked (SDK max_retries=2 inside middleware max_retries=2) and there is no per-request wall-clock cap; the adport client aborts at 240s and reports a false 'engine unreachable' while the engine keeps running the turn uncancelled (C11-03, C11-04).
No per-thread concurrency control or idempotency key: concurrent/retried POSTs race the LangGraph checkpointer on the same thread_id (C11-05).
A Pipeboard MCP outage at catalog load is silently swallowed to an empty/partial tool surface, loaded once per process, with /health still reporting ok (C11-06).

The mutation path is genuinely robust against duplicate submissions (single attempt, no retry on timeout, idempotency key, claim consumption, idempotent re-execute, reconciling readback) — but it is unreachable in the product (ProposalOnlyWriteProvider) and its contract tests are currently red due to a stale KILL_SWITCH file (C11-07, D1).

findings.title: Human approval not enforced on adport REST/MCP write surfaces (only the dashboard)
findings.description: The two-step validate->apply guardedWriteTool is satisfiable by the SAME principal on the REST (/api/v1/tools/{tool}) and MCP (/mcp) surfaces with no second human and no server-side interrupt. The MCP 'approval:{arguments}' object is an advisory structuredContent hint, not enforcement. The product 'human approval' invariant holds only in the markting dashboard apply route. An autonomous AI holding a tools:write key can validate then immediately apply a real ad-platform mutation within policy rails only.
findings.recommendation: Enforce an out-of-band human approver on apply for REST/MCP, or explicitly scope/document tools:write keys as self-service-within-rails and restrict who/what may hold them.

findings.title: Non-atomic pending consumption + no idempotency key: concurrent/duplicate apply can execute a live mutation twice
findings.description: PolicyEngine.apply does get->applyWrite->delete with no lock/transaction; PostgresPendingStore.delete is an unconditional UPDATE consumed_at=now() with no 'and consumed_at is null' and no row-count check; applyWrite takes no idempotency key. Two concurrent apply calls for one pending id both pass the unconsumed read and both call provider.applyWrite. The sandbox has a state CAS mitigation; live providers have none.
findings.recommendation: Consume atomically (UPDATE ... WHERE consumed_at IS NULL RETURNING, treat 0 rows as not-found), add SELECT FOR UPDATE across get+apply, and pass the pending id as a provider idempotency key.

findings.title: Dashboard self-approval guard bypassed for API-key-created pending ops; absent entirely on REST/MCP
findings.description: The guard is `if (row.createdBy && row.createdBy === principal.userId ...)`. authenticateApiKey returns a principal with no userId, so pending ops staged via an API key store created_by=null and the guard short-circuits, letting the same human approve their own API-key-staged change from the dashboard. The guard is also wholly absent on the REST/MCP apply paths.
findings.recommendation: Propagate the key owner's user id (or key id) into created_by and compare against it; default-deny when provenance is unknown unless MARKTING_ALLOW_SELF_APPROVAL=true.

findings.title: Budget-cap policy re-checked at validate but not at apply
findings.description: apply re-runs only checkStaticPolicy (protected accounts); checkBudgetPolicy runs only in validate. A budget cap tightened during the pending TTL window (default 15 min) is not enforced against an already-validated op.
findings.recommendation: Re-run checkBudgetPolicy inside apply against the current policy/preview.

Subsumes C5-01, C5-02, C4-01, C4-04, C8-08, C9-05. Verified in spot-checks 3, 4, 12.
findings.recommendation: Per-org (or per-thread) backend root, ArtifactStore and report index derived server-side from the thread id; CompositeBackend routing /conversation_history, /workspace, /large_tool_results to per-thread state; add read-deny for history/large-tool-results; enforce organization_id on /reports; contract test cross-thread ls/read_file is empty.

findings.title: Organization deletion and data retention never reach engine memory
findings.description: Org deletion cascades markting_* but never purges LangGraph checkpoints (verbatim user prose), pma_* proposals/receipts, or artifacts, which are keyed by a thread_id embedding the deleted org/user UUIDs. apply_data_retention omits markting_* and all engine tables; pma_dedupe has no TTL. A 'delete my org' request leaves the most sensitive memory in place indefinitely and the engine DB grows unbounded. Subsumes C4-02.
findings.recommendation: Add an engine purge endpoint (checkpointer.adelete_thread + pma_* + artifacts by org prefix) called from the deletion route; extend apply_data_retention to markting_* and engine tables (scheduled engine sweep by org prefix); add TTL on pma_dedupe.

findings.title: No token/cost metering and no spend quota anywhere in the stack
findings.description: grep usage_metadata/input_tokens/cache_control over engine/src returns nothing (spot-check 14/15). No per-org token or dollar ledger, no budget; plans carry no usage dimension; the only limiter is 120 req/min/user, a throughput limit. In live mode on one shared provider key a single seat can accrue hundreds of dollars/min (INFERRED). Subsumes C10-01, C10-02, C2-02, C12-03.
findings.recommendation: UsageMiddleware capturing usage_metadata per call -> pma_model_usage(org,user,thread,model,in,cached_in,out,cost); per-org monthly token/$ budget enforced in the cloud route (402 PLAN_LIMIT pattern); per-thread lifetime call cap; lower the assistant rate limit.

findings.title: No prompt caching and unbounded context growth (compaction only at ~850K tokens)
findings.description: resolve_model passes only timeout+max_retries; no cache_control is ever set, so the ~5.6K-token stable prefix and whole transcript are re-billed every call (spot-check 14). Compaction fires only at 85% of the 1M-token profile using the main model as summarizer; the UI reuses one thread per session, so turn cost grows linearly. Subsumes C10-03, C10-04, C9-09.
findings.recommendation: Ephemeral cache_control on system+tools and the last message (keep the date block last); explicit SummarizationMiddleware trigger ~60K tokens with a Haiku-class summarizer; new engine thread per conversation after N turns/idle.

findings.title: Model failures masked as HTTP-200 answers; all errors retried; no run deadline; client abort orphans the engine run
findings.description: ModelRetryMiddleware(on_failure=continue) returns an AIMessage 'Model call failed after N attempts...' (HTTP 200) on exhaustion; default_retry_on retries every non-ModelError (config/ValueError), wasting the budget and masking deterministic bugs. There is no per-run or per-request wall-clock deadline; the cloud aborts the fetch at 240s but does not cancel the engine, which keeps spending. Subsumes C11-01, C11-02, C11-03, C11-04, C1-04, C2-03, C10-05. Verified in spot-check 13.
findings.recommendation: Propagate a typed failure (code+localized message) instead of on_failure=continue; narrow retry_on to transient classes (429/5xx/timeout); add a run-level asyncio.wait_for deadline aligned below the client timeout; cancel on client disconnect; return a resumable turn id.

findings.title: No per-thread concurrency control or idempotency on chat; non-atomic live apply can execute a mutation twice
findings.description: Thread claim is ownership, not a mutex; two concurrent POST /threads/{id}/messages race the checkpoint. On the adport side apply is get->applyWrite->delete with no lock/transaction and no idempotency key into applyWrite; only the sandbox provider has a CAS, so two concurrent applies of one pending_operation_id can both execute a live mutation. Subsumes C11-05, C1-03, C13-02. Verified in spot-check 7.
findings.recommendation: Per-thread asyncio/advisory lock + client idempotency key on the message route (409 on a second in-flight turn); atomic consume (update ... where consumed_at is null returning *) with FOR UPDATE across get+apply; pass the pending id as a provider idempotency key.

findings.title: Demo engine mis-routes analysis questions to a hard-coded budget-cut proposal and shares scripted state across threads/tenants
findings.description: The default-mode scripted engine routes any message matching a keyword regex (incl. the product's own suggestion chip and Arabic negation particles غير/زد) to a write script that always proposes g-103 -> 240 regardless of the question, staging it into adport's production approval queue; and its state is one process-global instance, so a second thread/tenant gets 'exhausted' text or a malformed write turn. Demo code reaching the production approval path. Subsumes C3-04, C6-01, C6-02, C8-01, C8-02, C1-07.
findings.recommendation: Key script state by thread_id or construct a model per thread; restrict the write script to an explicit demo phrase or classify on imperative verbs excluding negations; add a two-thread host test and a test that every non-change suggestion chip yields no proposal.

findings.title: Account scoping checks one argument; cross-account reads possible; engine trusts readOnlyHint for direct tool binding
findings.description: The cloud authorizer checks only top-level account_id/customer_id, so Reddit/TikTok single-resource reads and Apple unscoped reads can cross accounts under one grant. The engine picks the first matching account_arg name and does not walk nested/list id args. The engine classifies any tool with readOnlyHint:true as READ and binds it directly, so a misannotated/malicious Pipeboard tool named update_*/upload_* becomes a direct model call (deny-name covers only mutate|raw|delete|remove|purge). Subsumes C7-04, C7-05, C7-06.
findings.recommendation: Wrap all provider tools (reads included) in AccountScopedProvider with per-tool scope extractors; make Apple account_id required; add verb-based deny patterns for READ classification and pin the read-catalog revision.

findings.title: Self-approval guard bypassed for API-key-created pending operations; guard absent on REST/MCP
findings.description: The dashboard requester-cannot-approve guard is `if (row.createdBy && row.createdBy === principal.userId ...)`; an API-key principal has no userId, so created_by is null and the guard short-circuits, letting the same human approve. The guard is also wholly absent on REST/MCP (see C14-P1-01). Separation of duties degrades to one person whenever the request originates from an API key. Subsumes C13-03. Verified in spot-check 8.
findings.recommendation: Propagate the key owner's user id / key id into created_by and compare against it; default-deny when provenance is unknown unless MARKTING_ALLOW_SELF_APPROVAL=true; move the switch into organization policy.

findings.title: Secret redaction misses JSON-quoted credential keys and common token shapes
findings.description: The credential regex requires the key immediately followed by :/=, so {"access_token":"..."} never matches; Meta EAA tokens, Google ya29., JWTs, AWS AKIA, and URL/base64-encoded configured secrets pass unredacted (6/13 shapes in C8's runtime probe). Provider error envelopes and provider_result previews are JSON, the most likely echo form. Reaches the checkpoint and artifact store. Live-mode only (fixtures carry no credentials). Subsumes C8-04.
findings.recommendation: Allow an optional quote between key and separator; add shape patterns for Meta/Google-OAuth/JWT/AWS and encoded variants of configured secrets; add negative tests; also route any future logs/traces through redact().

findings.title: No end-to-end tracing, correlation id, per-turn structured logging, or durable read audit on the self-hosted path
findings.description: No correlation id is minted or forwarded cloud->engine; LangSmith/OTel tracing is never enabled and the only tracing_context call disables it; there is no per-turn log of model/tokens/latency/tool-calls (5 log sites total); the read audit is an in-memory 500-entry ring consumed only by the demo. Incidents cannot be reconstructed per request/tenant. Subsumes C12-01, C12-02, C12-04, C12-05.
findings.recommendation: Mint a request id at the cloud edge, forward it, bind into logs + RunnableConfig.metadata + every audit/provenance row; enable one tracing backend tagged by org/user/thread with redaction on the sink; persist a durable read-audit; emit per-turn structured logs.

findings.title: Oversized deterministic results offload to an unusable stub (no path, no consumer); model can read the whole engine checkout
findings.description: summarize_window is unbounded (14,401 chars for 3 fixture accounts) and crosses the 6,000-char offload cliff; the stub carries no path and no deterministic tool consumes a tool_result artifact, so the numbers are lost and the skill forbids computing from previews. Separately, the filesystem read policy denies only secrets and allows everything else, so the model can grep/read src, tests, docs and instructions.md (its own prompt). Subsumes C9-01, C5-04, C9-05. Verified in spot-check 4.
findings.recommendation: Bounded head + analysis artifact for summarize_window/compare_periods; add read_analysis_section tool; put path+kind in the offload stub; invert the filesystem policy to allow only /skills and /workspace/{analysis,out}.

findings.title: Engine-side outcome memory is systematically wrong: every bridged proposal is recorded as rejected
findings.description: After a successful preview the bridge calls reject on the engine proposal ('handled by adport'), so the engine's durable conversation memory and the resumed graph record a rejection while the real outcome lives only in adport and is never fed back. A follow-up 'did my change go through?' is answered from a checkpoint that says rejected. No accepted/rejected learning is possible from engine data. Subsumes C4-05, C8-05.
findings.recommendation: Replace reject with a handed_off decision (or a reject message the system prompt interprets as 'pending in adport'); write the adport outcome back into the thread as a system message on the next turn.

findings.title: Model filesystem write covers artifacts/reports/kill-switch; artifact integrity is SHA-256 not HMAC
findings.description: write/edit are always bound and /workspace/** is writable except /workspace/skills, so the model can create the kill switch (halting all writes, with no delete tool to clear it), overwrite a served rpt_*.html, or attempt a forged performance_rows artifact. Artifact integrity is a plain SHA-256 stored next to the payload, not a host-keyed HMAC. Subsumes C7-07.
findings.recommendation: Deny model writes to /workspace/{analysis,in,out} and the kill-switch path; give a dedicated notes dir; sign artifacts with a host HMAC key.

findings.title: Budget cap re-check skipped at apply; 'expired' outcome never written and no sweep runs
findings.description: apply() re-runs checkStaticPolicy (protected accounts) only, not checkBudgetPolicy, so a validated op can land after a tightened budget cap within the 15-min TTL. The pending sweep that would set 'expired' is never invoked, so markting_engine_proposals.status sticks at pending and dashboards over-count. Subsumes C13-04, C12-07. Verified in spot-check 9.
findings.recommendation: Re-run checkBudgetPolicy inside apply; schedule the pending sweep to set expired and mark the provenance row.

findings.title: Three inconsistent write vocabularies/units exposed to AI clients
findings.description: Engine propose_change uses field->value in account currency/day; adport typed budgets use micros/cents/float per provider; the generic *_api_* tools add raw API fields; statuses use four vocabularies. The unit lives only in the tool description, not the schema, and the bridge reconciles only two operations for six providers. An LLM choosing between tiktok_set_budget{240} and tiktok_api_update{budget:240000000} has no schema-level unit guard. Subsumes C7-09.
findings.recommendation: Normalize to one money representation (amount + currency, integer minor units) on the tool boundary and convert inside providers; remove typed/generic duplication for agents.

findings.title: Advertised providers not installed in the engine image; implicit LANGSMITH_GATEWAY reroute contradicts 'no implicit gateway'
findings.description: The compose image installs only self-host/slack/reports extras, so Google/Groq/xAI/Mistral/DeepSeek presets crash at init_chat_model in the container though they work in the dev venv. Separately, the installed langchain reroutes anthropic:/openai: traffic through the LangSmith gateway whenever LANGSMITH_GATEWAY is truthy, contradicting config.py:24/assembly.py:154 ('no implicit gateway'). Subsumes C2-01, C2-07.
findings.recommendation: Either extend the image with intended extras or trim the advertised presets in markting docs; pin LANGSMITH_GATEWAY empty in compose and document it, or adopt the gateway explicitly.

findings.title: Engine test suite is not hermetic (stray workspace/KILL_SWITCH reddens 16-19 write-flow tests); no model-behaviour regression in CI
findings.description: The host writes engine/workspace/KILL_SWITCH at the default relative path resolved against project root; conftest pins model/workspace/approvers but not the kill-switch path, so after one host boot 16-19 write-flow and behaviour tests fail with reason kill_switch; they pass (30/30) when the path is isolated. Root Makefile does not run the engine suite and no model-behaviour regression runs in CI. Test-isolation defect, not a product defect; it means the write guarantees are currently unverified by a green run in this checkout. Subsumes C1-06, C4-08, C6-03, C6-06, C10-09, C11-07, C13-05. Confirmed by every cohort member and spot-checks 1/3.
findings.recommendation: Point the kill-switch path at a per-test tmp dir in conftest (as the demo tests already do); have the host engage the switch under its own workspace root; add the engine + engine-demo suites to root make test and a behaviour-regression job.

findings.title: Evaluation harness weak: q02 expectation disagrees with fixtures; 12/15 questions have no machine check; no provenance/hallucination grader
findings.description: q02 expect says 'google CPA 26.82 vs 29.60' while the shipped fixtures yield 25.80/28.13 or 26.04/27.97 (C6 VERIFIED_RUNTIME; spot-check 15 confirms the expect text). grade.py checks spend for q01/q05 only; CPA is never checked; 12/15 questions print 'numbers ok' whenever no error occurs; substring matching rejects formatted figures; no check that prose numbers originate from tool outputs, no refusal/tool-trace grader. A green run is weak evidence. Subsumes C6-04, C6-05, C6-08.
findings.recommendation: Generate every numeric expectation from compute.py over the fixtures; add a deterministic provenance grader (prose numbers must appear in tool outputs), tool-trace and refusal checks; record full transcripts; run graders in CI without a model key.

findings.title: No durable/tenant/account/long-term/outcome memory or learning
findings.description: No LangGraph store is configured, no memory.py exists, and the MDA memory the docs describe is off and deployment-global (unsuitable for multi-tenant by the upstream's own warning). measurement_plan/reversal_plan are parsed and stored but nothing schedules a measurement or records an outcome. Every conversation starts from zero knowledge of the org's goals, past recommendations, acceptance, or results. This is the core of the Marketing Memory and outcome-loop design. Subsumes C4-11, C5-06. No code claims otherwise, so GAP not defect.
findings.recommendation: Build tenant/account/decision memory in adport Postgres (RLS by org); governed learning restricted to user-confirmed facts, measured outcomes, and accept/reject rates used only to annotate/rank - never to change policy limits or approver sets. See 03-ai-evolution-plan.md sections 3 and 6.

findings.title: Arabic-first applies to UI chrome only; no language/locale policy, Arabic corpus, Arabic reports, or regional playbooks
findings.description: The prompt layer contains no Arabic and no language directive; the wiki is generic/English/US-centric with no Gulf calendar (Ramadan/Eid/White Friday), SAR/AED, RTL, or Snapchat/TikTok playbooks; the demo composer answers Arabic questions in English; reports hard-code lang=en and DejaVu fonts. The product is marketed as Arabic-first but that scopes to the Next.js UI. Subsumes C3-05, C5-05, C8-03, C6-09, C9-12.
findings.recommendation: Add a product-owned locale policy via build_agent_components(system_prompt=...) (answer in the user's language, Latin digits, ad terms in English, currency code after the number); bilingual regional wiki + Snap/TikTok playbooks; Arabic/RTL report template and fonts; bilingual eval set.

findings.title: Tool coverage gaps for a real media buyer (no creative/frequency reads, no change history, no Snap/TikTok/Pinterest/LinkedIn engine fixtures, no deterministic decomposition/anomaly tools)
findings.description: Engine reads expose spend/impressions/clicks/conversions/value only - no frequency, reach, creative id or age - so 'creative fatigue vs audience saturation' cannot be grounded; admitted writes are budget/status for three fixture platforms; deterministic analysis is compare_periods/summarize_window/render_report with no ROAS decomposition, significance test, or marginal-efficiency curve. The code does not claim these, so GAP. Subsumes C7-16, C6-10.
findings.recommendation: Add creative/frequency reads and normalizers for all providers, a deterministic explain_delta (value vs spend vs mix), significance testing, change-history reads, and Snap/TikTok/Pinterest/LinkedIn engine fixtures so eval and the bridge have engine-side data.

key_findings: Verdict, proven from capabilities: markting-ai is a dashboard-with-chat over synthetic data, not an intelligent operating system - the host refuses live credentials and pins sample mode in both demo and live, so every 'analysis' a tenant sees is fixture data (serve_demo.py:139-171,383-392).

The central safety invariant holds on the engine->bridge Assistant path (engine is fail-closed, proposal-only; 6 bypass attempts blocked and verified) but is BROKEN on adport's own REST/MCP write surfaces: any tools:write holder can validate then apply with no human (P1; checks 5,6).

The engine receives {text} + fixtures and zero tenant/business/margin/market/currency/locale/history context; the only tenant-context mechanism is absent, Git-ignored and deployment-global (P1; checks 1,11).

Cross-tenant isolation holes exist by construction in the model's shared state - summarization writes verbatim history to world-readable /conversation_history, one shared /workspace+ArtifactStore, and a global report index served to any bearer - latent now (fixtures), P0 on live reads (P1; checks 3,4,12).
Generic *_api_* write tools let an agent make uncapped status/bid/targeting/destructive changes with budget-only policy (P1; check 10).

No memory, no learning, no outcome loop: no LangGraph store, every bridged proposal recorded as rejected, org deletion/retention never reach engine memory, measurement_plan stored but never measured (P1/P2/GAP).

No metering, no quota, no prompt caching, compaction only at ~850K tokens, model failures masked as HTTP-200 answers, no run deadline, no per-thread concurrency control - the operability floor for live mode is near zero (P2).

All 15 spot-checked citations held (14 CONFIRMED, 1 PARTIAL); the C1-C13 cohort's code-level evidence is reliable and cross-corroborating, with soft spots (live model, Docker, Postgres concurrency, MDA) honestly self-flagged.
C14.disagreements: "Code contradicts several documented claims, all VERIFIED_CODE: (1) README.md:79 'nothing is applied until a human approves it' - true only for the Assistant; adport REST/MCP apply writes with no enforced human approver (write.ts:40-156, v1/tools route, mcp/index.ts). (2) docs listing company-context and 'read business context' as a shipped capability (capability-map.md:18) - the folder is absent, Git-ignored and never created per org. (3) 'Analyses connected accounts' / 'Arabic-first' reasoning (README) - the engine only ever sees USD fixtures and no language reaches the model. (4) config.py:24 / assembly.py:154 'no implicit gateway' - installed langchain reroutes through LANGSMITH_GATEWAY when the env var is set. (5) tools-and-context.md:48 'cannot read coding-agent files or paths outside its root' - the model can read the whole engine checkout incl. its own prompt. (6) markting_engine_proposals.status enum advertises 'expired' but no code writes it. (7) PHASE0-REPORT 'engine suite 177 passed' is reproducible only on a clean workspace - a stray KILL_SWITCH reddens 16-19 tests in this checkout. One inter-report disagreement I adjudicated: C5 rates the summarization cross-tenant leak P0 'by construction, latent in default config'; I consolidated it to P1 because it requires live mode + long threads + two orgs on one process to coincide - C5's framing is defensible and noted."
C14.not_verified: "As lead I re-confirmed 15 static citations (14 CONFIRMED, 1 PARTIAL - the q02 fixture-figure mismatch inherits C6's VERIFIED_RUNTIME grade.window_totals, which I did not re-run) but re-ran no pytest/vitest suites; cited test exit codes are the specialists' (C1/C4/C6/C7/C13), which cross-agree on the kill-switch root cause. Inherited NOT_VERIFIED from the cohort, needing resources an audit must not use: live-model behaviour (MARKTING_ENGINE_MODE=live, no key) - Arabic answers, injection susceptibility, real live-turn shape and cost (C10 dollar figures rest on an assumed price table + chars/4 heuristic and are INFERRED, not fact); the Docker image contents (builds blocked); Postgres/Supabase concurrency - the double-apply race and JSONB-CAS are VERIFIED_CODE, not reproduced; the MDA hosted path (Context Hub, platform checkpointer, MANAGED_RECURSION_LIMIT); live Pipeboard catalog schemas (so the readOnlyHint-trust and account-arg findings are mechanism-level); whether any deployment cron invokes the pending sweep; and the main open architecture question for the forward plan - whether routing live reads through adport's tenant runtime fits the engine's process-global profile (assembly.py:189-195) without one engine process per tenant."
